How this is worked out
  • Dropped first: the platform whose lower price was seen at the earliest crawl. If two platforms dropped in the same 10-minute crawl window, both are shown as dropping at the same time.
  • Followed: the other platform was seen at its old price after the first drop, then dropped in a later crawl. Didn’t follow: it was crawled again and kept its price. No later crawl: the first drop happened at the last crawl, so there’s nothing to compare yet.
  • Recovered: the platform’s price went back up to (or above) what it was before its drop. The time shown is the crawl where that was first seen.
  • 2nd, 3rd drop: once a price has recovered, the next drop on that platform starts a new drop, with its own recovery check. Further cuts before the price recovers count as part of the same drop.
  • When stock_status is out_of_stock (or the price is 0), that crawl is treated as out of stock: its price is ignored and never counted as a drop or a recovery. Prices are compared with the last in-stock price. Only selling_price is used; lowest_selling_price is ignored. Times are crawl times, so the real change happened some time in the 10 minutes before.
  • Response time: for each price drop on one platform (a fresh drop, not a further cut before the price recovered), the time until the other platform next changed its price, for the same SKU or, if chosen, any product in the same sub-category. It’s measured between crawls, so the real reaction happened somewhere between the previous crawl and the one shown. “Same crawl” means both prices changed between the same two crawls, so we can’t tell which came first. Drops where the other platform wasn’t crawled again with a price are left out.
  • Time range: everything is worked out again using only the crawls in the chosen range, so a drop is “first” within that range, and recovery is checked only up to its last crawl.
  • Filters on the SKU page narrow the list; the number next to each option is how many SKUs it would leave, given the other filters.
  • Categories: amazon.in and flipkart.com name their categories differently, so pick whose names to use. A SKU not categorised on that platform uses the other platform’s category. Category columns (primary_category_name, test_sub_category_1–4) are optional; “-” counts as empty.
  • Platforms are shown by domain, taken from each row’s product_url (www. is dropped, so https://www.amazon.in/… becomes amazon.in). If a row has no usable URL, the domain is worked out from site_name, e.g. amazon_in_… becomes amazon.in.
  • SKUs are matched across platforms by internal_company_sku. A CSV needs crawl_timestamp, product_url or site_name, selling_price and internal_company_sku (or product_name). Loaded files stay in your browser.
